hooks.text: A galaxy-sized cosmic cloud isn't a star.
Astronomers found a glowing gas cloud three times wider than our galaxy.
Three hundred thousand light-years across, a giant space cloud glows in the dark.

title: The Cosmic Fog Bank
description: Discover Lyman-alpha blob 1, an enormous cloud of glowing hydrogen gas hiding two colliding galaxies at its center.

beats.text: A galaxy-sized cosmic cloud isn't a star.
beats.visual: Wide field image of Lyman-alpha blob 1 by the Very Large Telescope, 2011

beats.text: Astronomers scanned the distant universe and stumbled upon this monster in 2000.
beats.visual: The Very Large Telescope at night on Paranal Observatory, 2015

beats.text: Scientists spent over fifteen years debating what powers its eerie light.
beats.visual: Comparison diagram of LAB-1 size versus Milky Way, 2020

beats.text: Polarized measurements revealed that the massive blob doesn't actually glow on its own.
beats.visual: Visual of light polarization in a ring diagram, 2018

beats.text: Hidden at its heart are two galaxies colliding and churning out new stars.
beats.visual: Illustration of two galaxies merging artist's impression, 2020

beats.text: Their intense light scatters through the gas like streetlights in a foggy night.
beats.visual: Foggy night streetlight for analogy photograph, 2019

beats.text: That giant celestial fog bank shines far beyond the Milky Way.
beats.visual: Wide field image of Lyman-alpha blob 1 by the Very Large Telescope, 2011
